A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OCTAX platform and provide readable main texts, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The original environment-generation appendix moves from E to F; its generated game and wrapper code is retained.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPO experiments across 16 games, throughput measurements against EnvPool, a Pong hyperparameter search, and training on three generated Target Shooter levels.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds PQN experiments and an evaluation of LLM-generated score and termination functions across 21 games.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 introduces optional no-op-reset and sticky-action wrappers, extending the available reset and action procedures. The core CHIP-8 emulator and seven-step environment-generation pipeline remain unchanged. Expanded game descriptions do not establish further implementation changes.

E1.justification: Gameplay evaluation retains the same 16 games and three Target Shooter levels. Appendix E adds systematic reward/termination extraction from undocumented assembly across all 21 games, extending the evaluated task coverage beyond v1's anecdotal account of LLM assistance.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 expand the main learning evaluation from PPO alone to PPO versus Parallel Q-Network (PQN) across all 16 games. EnvPool remains the comparator in the separate throughput experiment.

E3.justification: The new LLM study introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: assembly without symbolic information or documentation, access restricted to 16 registers, human-written reference functions, and four matching categories. PQN experiments add LayerNorm, lambda 0.9, and epsilon-greedy decay from 1 to 0.05 during the first 10% of training. Existing PPO and throughput protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E systematically analyzes LLM extraction failures, including score encoding, register confusion, and missed compound termination conditions, with per-game examples. This substantially extends the earlier anecdotal discussion. The existing Pong hyperparameter analysis and Target Shooter difficulty study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 12 training seeds, IQM curves with 10th–90th percentile ranges and confidence intervals, and 50 throughput measurements per configuration. PQN uses the existing reporting practice; the new LLM study introduces no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds PQN learning curves for all 16 games. New Table 3 reports per-game extraction outcomes, including 12/21 perfect score functions and 4/21 perfect termination functions. Existing throughput results, all 18 hyperparameter-search rows, and Target Shooter results are unchanged. Table 3's non-perfect score-category totals conflict with its individual rows.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The additional register rules, implementation descriptions, and empirical matching categories do not introduce a theoretical derivation or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the Atari positioning: the abstract describes an alternative to Atari games rather than the Atari benchmark, and the introduction explicitly excludes a drop-in replacement. The central claims about accelerated emulation, diverse learning challenges, and LLM-assisted generation remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix E replace an unqualified account of successful LLM extraction with substantive limitations: complex scoring and termination require human verification, and implementation matching does not establish semantic equivalence. Section 3.3 also adds a qualification concerning modular rewards and ALE-style human-normalized scoring.

D1.justification: Appendix C expands brief game descriptions into detailed action mappings, reward registers, termination conditions, and ROM-modification descriptions across the suite. v3 also supplies the extraction-study prompt and PQN settings. These substantially improve documentation, although the newly listed Brix termination condition contradicts Section 3.3.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gallici et al. (2024) to support the PQN comparison and explicitly qualifies OCTAX's relationship to ALE. The broader related-work coverage and positioning within JAX environment research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the experimental discussion, expanded game explanations, corrected cross-references, and new acknowledgments and appendix subsections. The main narrative order and most existing prose remain intact; the generation appendix is renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR page template, changing text width, heading typography, running headers, and figure placement throughout. Figure 3 adds PQN curves, a method legend, and rescaled axes; a color-coded Table 3 is added. The existing generation pipeline, screenshot, and difficulty plot are reordered and resized.

improvement.justification: The PQN comparison broadens evidence beyond one learner, while Appendices C and E improve implementation transparency and qualify LLM capabilities with measured failures. These gains are moderated by new inconsistencies: Brix terminates at V[14]=4 in Appendix C but zero in Section 3.3, and Table 3 lists two Wrong Logic and four Failure score rows while reporting three of each. The revision is more informative, but these defects limit the overall improvement.
